text:
mike: ALERT: discovered presigned S3 URLs in backup logs that include an old service account key for `model-cache-writer`. Possible exfil of backup snapshots. DO NOT restore from suspicious backups. We're treating this as potential credential exposure and rotating immediately.

sso-bot: Incident created: INC-5400  Pager: @oncall_engsec  https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-5400 :rotating_light:

olga: Confirmed in logs: recent PUTs to s3://model-cache-backups/ with auth header using AccessKeyId AKIAEXAMPLEOLD1234, last used 2026-06-10T03:12Z. I can reproduce a presigned URL pattern in the backup metadata.

chandra: Short-term containment plan:
- revoke the old access key immediately (console + IaC)
- rotate any KMS data keys used by cache-writer and re-encrypt targets where feasible
- disable presigned URL generation service until new credentials and tighter signing policy are in place
- scan S3 for objects created with presigned URLs and quarantine suspicious snapshots

dave: Longer-term: we should move to an STS-based flow for model-cache writes (short-lived role assumption), reduce S3 permissions to a narrow prefix, and add object-level encryption with separate KMS keys per-customer. I'll open infra tasks for least-privilege migration.

olga: I'm revoking the key now. Command run: `aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLEOLD1234 --status Inactive --user-name svc-cache-writer` then scheduling deletion after verification. Also starting a bucket inventory scan: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket model-cache-backups --query 'Contents[?contains(Key, `snapshot`)]'`.

support-eng: Notifying CS/SOC with the draft advisory for Dedicated customers who pull backups. Draft posted to #customer-success/drafts: https://docs.redwood/drafts/backup-key-exposure.md  Please review customer-facing wording.

mike: Assignments: olga add scan results to INC-5400, chandra disable presign service and coordinate new signing policy, dave open infra RFC for STS migration, support-eng finalize customer notice. Meeting in 20m in #eng-security to confirm containment and external disclosure timeline. :exclamation:
